cards.name: Opacity - 20%
cards.summary: Keyboard command (Tools set of Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts, no key assigned by default) that is expected to set the opacity of the selected objects to 20%, the same as typing 20 in the Transparency panel's Opacity field, so 80% of what lies behind shows through. The harvest did not run it live, so the exact target (whole object vs. a targeted appearance row) is unconfirmed.
use_for: ghosted background shapes and oversized numerals behind poster headlines
faint watermark logos on proofs and mockups
light texture or pattern shapes laid over a photo
avoid: body text or thin lines that must stay readable: 20% is too faint; use a lighter solid color instead

print with spot colors or overprint: transparency is flattened when printed or saved as EPS or an older PDF standard; a solid tint of the swatch prints more predictably (check with Window > Flattener Preview)
expecting a default key: none is assigned; set one under Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts > Tools first
cards.how: Assign a key first: Edit > Keyboard Shortcuts, Tools set, find 'Opacity - 20%' and type a shortcut. Then select objects (Selection tool, or target a group) and press it; the Transparency panel (Window > Transparency) should read 20%. Set blend mode or knockout options in that panel. In CorelDRAW the matching Uniform Transparency counts the other way: 80 transparency = 20% opacity.
cards.script_api: No invoke for "Adobe Opacity 20" in the harvest (it is a command, and the app.selectTool probe never reached it). Same result by DOM: for each item in app.activeDocument.selection set item.opacity = 20 (PageItem.opacity, 0-100); a whole layer: Layer.opacity = 20.

review.changes: avoid: 'flattened on output' narrowed to printing / EPS / older PDF (native .ai and PDF/X-4 keep live transparency)

cards.name: Presentation Mode
cards.summary: Shows the document as a full-screen slideshow: the interface disappears and each artboard fills the screen on a black background, one at a time in artboard order; arrow keys move between artboards and Esc exits. Same command as View > Presentation Mode; the artwork is not changed.
use_for: presenting logo options, a brand-guideline deck or a multi-artboard campaign to a client from the .ai file
a clean full-screen check of each social post or ad size
reviewing composition and balance artboard by artboard without UI clutter
avoid: sharing with someone without Illustrator: save a PDF or export the artboards as PNG / JPG
checking bleed or art outside the artboard: presentation shows the artboard area only; use the normal view
editing: nothing can be selected or changed while presenting; press Esc first
pressing Shift+F while editing text: it types a capital F; press Esc first
cards.how: Arrange and number the artboards in the Artboards panel first (that sets the slide order). With a document open (View > Presentation Mode is disabled without one in the harvest's menu walk), press Shift+F with no text being edited, or choose View > Presentation Mode. Right / Left arrow keys step through the artboards; Esc returns to the normal window.
cards.script_api: No DOM call. The harvest has no app.selectTool result for "Adobe Presentation Mode", and the menu item View/Presentation Mode has no executeMenuCommand id (only its menu path and Win32 command 397), and the harvested ScreenMode enum (MULTIWINDOW, DESKTOP, FULLSCREEN) has no presentation value. A pipeline that needs a slideshow exports the artboards instead (Document.exportFile per artboard, or Document.saveAs PDF).

review.changes: how: needs an open document (ai_menu harvest enabled_without_document false); script_api: added harvested Win32 command 397 and that ScreenMode has no presentation value

cards.name: Show/Hide All But Toolbox
cards.summary: Hides every open panel except the toolbar (and the Control panel when it is shown), and brings them back on the next press; the artwork is untouched. A hidden docked panel pops out when the pointer hovers over the strip at the window edge where it was docked.
use_for: more drawing room on a laptop screen while keeping the tools at hand
cleaner screen recordings and tutorials that still show tool changes
focused drawing or lettering sessions with the panels out of the way
avoid: pressing it while editing text: Shift+Tab goes to the text; press Esc first
hiding the toolbar as well: use Tab (Show/Hide All Palettes)
showing artwork to a client: Presentation Mode (Shift+F) hides all interface and shows only the artboards
cards.how: Press Shift+Tab with no text being edited (Esc first if a type cursor is active). Press it again to restore the panels. Hover at the screen edge to reach a hidden docked panel without restoring all of them.
cards.script_api: No DOM call for panel visibility in the harvest, and the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Toggle Closing Palettes". Scripts do not need panels hidden or shown.

review.changes: summary: dropped the unsupported 'Auto-Show Hidden Panels in Preferences > User Interface' setting (a Photoshop / InDesign preference)

cards.name: Show/Hide All Palettes
cards.summary: Hides all panels, including the toolbar, the Control panel and every docked panel, so only the document window and menu bar remain; the next press shows them again. The artwork is untouched.
use_for: the largest possible canvas for checking a full layout
quick screenshots of artwork without interface around it
keyboard-driven work where tool shortcuts replace the toolbar
avoid: pressing Tab while editing text: it types a tab character; press Esc first
keeping the toolbar visible: use Shift+Tab (Show/Hide All But Toolbox)
a client presentation: Presentation Mode (Shift+F) also hides the menu bar and shows artboards one at a time
cards.how: Press Tab with no text being edited (Esc first if a type cursor is active). Press Tab again to bring every panel back. Combine with F (screen modes) for an even cleaner view.
cards.script_api: No DOM call for panel visibility in the harvest, and the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Toggle Palettes". Scripts do not need panels hidden or shown.

cards.name: Swap Fill/Stroke
cards.summary: Exchanges the fill color and stroke color (solid, gradient or pattern) of the selected objects; with nothing selected it swaps the toolbar's Fill and Stroke boxes used for new art. Stroke weight and the other stroke settings are not swapped.
use_for: turning a solid shape into an outline-only version (or back) for line-icon or mono logo variants
quick fill / outline color inversions on badges, buttons and stickers
outlined headline treatments: swap a solid headline to stroke-only, then set the stroke weight
avoid: stroke weight surprises: the weight stays, so a shape that becomes stroke-only shows the old weight; set it after the swap
pressing it while editing text: it types a capital X; press Esc first
only changing which box is active: that is X (Toggle Fill/Stroke)
resetting to white fill / black stroke: use D (Default)
cards.how: Select objects (or nothing, to set the colors for the next object) and press Shift+X, or click the small curved double arrow beside the Fill / Stroke boxes in the toolbar. Check the stroke weight in the Stroke or Properties panel afterwards.
cards.script_api: No invoke for "Adobe Swap Fill Stroke" in the harvest (the app.selectTool probe never reached it). Script the result instead: for each selected PathItem swap fillColor <-> strokeColor and filled <-> stroked (set strokeWidth yourself); type: TextRange.characterAttributes.fillColor / strokeColor; new art: swap Document.defaultFillColor / defaultStrokeColor and defaultFilled / defaultStroked.

review.changes: avoid: removed the invented '(often 1 pt)'; avoid: D named by its harvested name 'Default'

cards.name: Symbolism Tools - Decrease Intensity
cards.summary: While a Symbolism tool (Symbol Sprayer, Shifter, Scruncher, Sizer, Spinner, Stainer, Screener or Styler) is active, lowers the Intensity setting, so each pass sprays fewer instances or changes them more gently. It changes the tool setting only, not the artwork.
use_for: sparser sprays of stars, leaves, confetti or grass
small, controlled nudges to size, rotation or position of sprayed symbols
building tint (Stainer) or transparency (Screener) gradually in light passes
avoid: exact counts or placements: symbolism tools are brush-driven and random; place instances by hand or by script
a tablet with Use Pressure Pen on in the Symbolism Tools Options: pen pressure sets the intensity instead
changing the brush size: that is [ / ] (no Shift)
cards.how: Select the symbol set (the Symbol Sprayer can start a new one), pick a Symbolism tool and press Shift+{ (as the Keyboard Shortcuts dialog shows it; Shift+[ on a US keyboard) to lower Intensity; the current value is in the Symbolism Tools Options dialog (double-click any Symbolism tool). [ and ] change the brush diameter instead.
cards.script_api: No DOM access to the Symbolism tool options in the harvest, and the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Symbolism Dec Intensity". A script builds the result directly instead of spraying: Document.symbolItems.add(symbol) per instance, then position, resize, rotate and opacity on each SymbolItem for a controlled, repeatable set.

review.changes: how: batch shortcut Shift+{ stated first; Shift+[ marked as the US-layout key

cards.name: Symbolism Tools - Increase Intensity
cards.summary: While a Symbolism tool (Symbol Sprayer, Shifter, Scruncher, Sizer, Spinner, Stainer, Screener or Styler) is active, raises the Intensity setting, so each pass sprays more instances or changes them faster and harder. It changes the tool setting only, not the artwork.
use_for: dense fills of a background with bubbles, stars or foliage in a few strokes
strong one-pass changes with the Sizer, Spinner or Shifter on large symbol sets
bold staining or screening when a quick, visible change is wanted
avoid: subtle edits: high intensity overshoots; lower it (Shift+{) or work in short dabs
heavy files: dense sprays add many instances; a pattern swatch or scatter brush can be lighter
a tablet with Use Pressure Pen on in the Symbolism Tools Options: pen pressure sets the intensity instead
cards.how: Select the symbol set (the Symbol Sprayer can start a new one), pick a Symbolism tool and press Shift+} (as the Keyboard Shortcuts dialog shows it; Shift+] on a US keyboard) to raise Intensity; the current value is in the Symbolism Tools Options dialog (double-click any Symbolism tool). [ and ] change the brush diameter instead.
cards.script_api: No DOM access to the Symbolism tool options in the harvest, and the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Symbolism Inc Intensity". A script builds the result directly instead of spraying: Document.symbolItems.add(symbol) per instance, then position, resize, rotate and opacity on each SymbolItem for a controlled, repeatable set.

review.changes: how: batch shortcut Shift+} stated first; Shift+] marked as the US-layout key

cards.name: Toggle Drawing Mode
cards.summary: Cycles the drawing mode shown at the bottom of the toolbar: Draw Normal (new art on top), Draw Behind (new art directly below the selected object, or at the back of the active layer when nothing is selected) and Draw Inside (new or placed art is clipped inside the one selected object, making a clipping group). Pressing it changes no artwork; the mode decides where the next objects land (in Draw Inside the selected object becomes the clipping path once you draw).
use_for: placing a photo or texture inside a shape or a headline (clipping without Make Clipping Mask)
painting shading and highlights inside an illustration shape with the Brush or Blob Brush
adding background elements behind finished art without reordering layers
avoid: forgetting the mode is on: later art keeps going behind or inside; check the toolbar icon and return to Draw Normal
Draw Inside with nothing or several objects selected: it needs exactly one path, compound path or text object; for groups use Object > Clipping Mask > Make
pressing Shift+D while editing text: it types a capital D; press Esc first
cards.how: Press Shift+D (no text being edited) to step Normal > Behind > Inside, or click the mode icons at the bottom of the toolbar. For Draw Inside select one path, compound path or text object first; dotted corner marks show the container. Draw, paint or File > Place into it, then press Shift+D until Draw Normal is back.
cards.script_api: No DOM property for the drawing mode in the harvest, and the app.selectTool probe never reached "Adobe Toggle Drawing Mode". Script the results: Draw Behind = create the item, then item.zOrder(ZOrderMethod.SENDBACKWARD) until it sits below the target, or SENDTOBACK; Draw Inside = put container and art in a GroupItem (container on top), set container.clipping = true and group.clipped = true; or select the art with the container on top and run app.executeMenuCommand("makeMask") (Object > Clipping Mask > Make, verified live in the harvest).

review.changes: summary: 'existing art is not changed' contradicted Draw Inside turning the selected object into a clipping path; script_api: added the harvested, live-verified makeMask executeMenuCommand route for Draw Inside
